title: Neuroplasticity and Brain Learning
text: Neuroplasticity refers to the brain's ability to reorganize itself by forming new neural connections throughout life in response to experience, learning, and injury. This phenomenon underlies learning and memory, recovery from brain injury, and adaptation to new environments. Long-term potentiation (LTP) is the cellular mechanism most associated with synaptic strengthening in learning. Hebbian learning describes how synapses are strengthened when neurons fire together repeatedly. Research has shown that the adult brain retains significant plasticity, challenging the earlier view that neural structure was fixed after childhood. Practices such as meditation, exercise, and learning new skills can promote beneficial neuroplastic changes.
